command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
review="$reports/review-specs.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-specs stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R2's Fix is wrong and its 'Fix risk: none' is false. The replacement sentence for specs/date-selection/spec.md:4 says '(a wall-time input keeps its status, see the time-selection capability)'. Design D2 rule 3 (design.md:80) says 'a Here entry target and the device time zone changed → the target is dropped, the status becomes UNIQUE', and specs/time-selection/spec.md:200-208 'A device time zone change ends the hint on the Here entry' agrees. With no home set, a device time zone change is a reference-zone change, so the fix writes a new contradiction into the spec. It should limit 'keeps its status' to a wall-time input on a location.

R4's Problem and Impact are contradicted by the existing code. src/test/features/locations/steps/locations_here_entry_data_unit.steps.tsx runs the legacy-zone scenario 'Renamed device time zone' (lines 147-178) inside a shared feature: it uses startOnOutdatedZoneData(), presents on engine.modules via presentHereEntryOnEngine, and its f.AfterEachScenario(() => { warmCheck.stop(); restoreZoneData(); }) (lines 33-36) undoes the stub, so the stub neither leaks nor goes unexercised. The real issue is only that task 6.1 should name this pattern (startOnOutdatedZoneData + fresh modules) instead of 'the stub of 2.2'. The proposed separate feature file is unnecessary, and WARNING is inflated.
